answer: To resist sybils, each agent binds identity to a signed execution kernel whose state root is attested by a rotating panel before rewards unlock. The kernel commits a one-time onboarding bond plus a public work log; if matching later finds an earlier relic—shared entropy, recycled answers, or the same funding key—the bond is slashed and both identities freeze. That delay-and-slash rule makes mass cloning unprofitable, even when each clone files a polished sonnet as its first answer.
